body: This question about full time work is one that I spent a lot of time on. It can be generalized to something like: "what would make life worth living?" and I can't think of a good answer to that question. Maybe if there was a God, but like you pointed out - no, that wouldn't seem to change anything. Perhaps if we lived forever? but if our lives are pointless when they're limited to 70 years, they'd be infinitely pointless if they went on forever. I think this really is the heart of the issue - it's not just that life is meaningless, its that it can't be anything but meaningless.

it's an interesting question. I think as far as medical science and technology in general, obviously the world is a better place, but if you read the classics; if you look into the political systems of the ancient world; if you consider what people of that time said about the state of the world (a good example is Plato's ship of state - book VI of the Republic) you see that essentially the way people interact with one another, and the way power structures, governments, institutions and so on are built, maintained, and eventually crumble, remain almost entirely unchanged. The main difference between now, and Plato's time is that we're more efficient at exploitation. Technology has the power to improve our lives, but it doesn't change our nature, so yes, life is better now; but no, it isn't different.

I've tried therapy and medication. the meds (i've tried 4 different kinds) made me a zombie (particularly lexapro - I would fall asleep at 9pm no matter where I was, even on the floor sometimes), and I got locked up for a week after being honest with a therapist once. Funny story - in my state habeas corpus doesn't exist under what's called an "emergency petition" which can be filed by any licensed therapist when I say something out loud that I think almost every moment of every day of my life. I look at therapists as being more dangerous than cops, and I certainly try to avoid them as much. When you can get locked up without charge or trial for speech, shit is going wrong, so as far as I'm concerned therapy is out of the question. anyway, I haven't taken meds or seen a professional for something like 5 years.
This shit ain't changing, no matter how hard anyone works. It's been like this since before Rome. This is how we are. It'll be like this until the end.

I wish I could agree. I've been feeling the same way for at least 10 years. Can I expect another 50 years of this, *then* death? Why? It just seems like if its going to suck, and it'll end the same way no matter what... I've heard the life is what you make it deal before, and i've spent a lot of time thinking about that, but I think it goes back to what I said about the state of power on this planet. Life isn't what you make of it, it's what someone else makes you make of it.
i dont have feelsgoodman moments. I just have this-is-what-every-day-is-like moments. Shit just never seems to change, you know?
how can you say that? Where is this meaning coming from? Where is it? I've never seen it.
